title: Code thinking length on CuteAFD: K4-Core-K6's 6-bit core against its BF16 core, 16 code prompts x 4 seeds
question: On code tasks on CuteAFD v4.0.0, does K4-Core-K6 with its native 6-bit core think longer than the same checkpoint with its BF16 core converted to FP8 at load?
engines: tpurtell/cuteafd v4.0.0 (coordinator image index sha256:e257bc61...), unmodified launcher
checkpoints: derived/GLM-5.3-Flash-EXL3-K4-Core-K6-BF16core @ 049c0180 (local derived checkpoint, not a producer release; built by results/2026-11-03-cuteafd-core-swap/prep/build_derived.py)
hardware: 2x NVIDIA RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell Max-Q Workstation Edition (300 W); GPU only, experts local

goals.question: Twelve new code projects (p4-p15) written before any request: does each reference implementation pass its hidden tests?

design.items: 16 projects: p0-p3 Block L code projects (byte-identical), p4-p15 written 2026-11-05

goals.headline: Each reference implementation passes its tests (README.md, PROTOCOL.md); p0-p3 are the Block L projects unchanged, p4-p15 new and the primary set.

goals.question: On the 12 new code prompts, does K4-Core-K6 with its native 6-bit core think longer than the same checkpoint with the BF16 core (FP8 at load) on CuteAFD v4.0.0?

design.instrument: free generation via the frozen v4 Block L stage-L3 driver (cap 130,048, 2 concurrent, thinking on, model default sampling); reasoning tokens by re-tokenization with the Block L analyzer; ratio = exp(mean seed-paired log(C-K6 / C-K6x))
arms: C-K6x (derived BF16-core checkpoint, BF16 converted to FP8 at load; same experts)
design.repeats: 4 replies per prompt per arm; seed 2,026,110,500 + 100 x prompt + rep, the same on both arms; one launch per arm
design.interval: 95% bootstrap over prompts (4,000 replicates, seed 20261105); detected when the interval excludes 1; sign test over prompts

goals.status_note: Reading revised by later runs: results/2026-11-06-vllm-code-thinking (same prompts on the vLLM fork: V-K6 / V-BF16 1.00 [0.96, 1.04], not detected; engine comparison 0.79 [0.75, 0.83]) and results/2026-11-06-cuteafd-fp8-ablation (switching off the BF16-core arm's FP8 KDA setting: F-kda / C-K6x 1.31 [1.24, 1.38]). The vLLM run describes the 1.26x as the FP8-at-load BF16 core thinking about 20% shorter than the other three configurations. CT-RESULT.md:32 ('The core accounts for the code gap seen in Block L') and :35 ('the native 6-bit core makes code replies think about 26% longer') predate these runs. CT-RESULT.md:37 says science-question free generation and the stop decision showed no core difference on CuteAFD; on CuteAFD only the stop decision was measured on science-question traces (core-swap S2, not detected, CS-stop-core); science-question free generation was measured only on the vLLM fork, on one question (2026-11-02-thinking-length G4).
goals.headline: C-K6 / C-K6x 1.26 [1.24, 1.29] over prompts (pairs [1.20, 1.33]); 12 of 12 prompts above 1, sign test p = 0.0005: detected. All 128 replies finished; none capped. CuteAFD v4.0.0; 'BF16 core' is BF16 converted to FP8 at load.
goals.superseded_by: 2026-11-06-vllm-code-thinking/ENGINES and 2026-11-06-cuteafd-fp8-ablation/STEPS (reading of the cause; the measured ratio stands)

goals.question: Secondary sets: all 16 prompts, and the four Block L prompts alone (against Block L 1.43 and core-swap step 1 1.25).

goals.headline: All 16: 1.33 [1.27, 1.40] (16 of 16 above 1, p = 3e-5). p0-p3: 1.56 [1.52, 1.62] (4 of 4, p = 0.125). C-K6 longer in 58 of 64 pairs; single pairs range 0.86 to 2.62.
